name: Toast Tables
description: Toast Tables is Toast's restaurant reservation, waitlist, experiences, guestbook, two-way messaging, floor-plan, table-status, server-rotation, seating, prepayment, and reporting product.
agentUseSummary: Toast Tables cannot yet be connected through Relay. Toast documents its general APIs and partner authentication, but does not publicly identify a Toast Tables reservation or waitlist API, scopes, schemas, webhooks, or standard-access contract. Relay needs Toast integration-partner approval, Tables-specific certification and credentials, explicit restaurant activation, and representative sandbox acceptance before exposing any reservation, guest, messaging, or table authority.

capabilities.label: Read reservations and waitlist
capabilities.description: After Toast approval, read only the contracted restaurant's reservations, experiences, waitlist, availability, guest requests, status, and booking metadata.

capabilities.label: Read table operations
capabilities.description: After Toast approval, read only the contracted floor plan, table and order status, server roster, rotations, covers, and seating state.

capabilities.label: Manage reservations and waitlist
capabilities.description: After Toast approval, create, update, seat, cancel, or message reservations and waitlist parties only under exact restaurant authority and explicit confirmation.

blocked.label: Connect before Toast approval
blocked.description: Relay has no Toast integration-partner account, Tables-specific scopes, assigned credentials, sandbox certification, production approval, or activated restaurant.

blocked.label: Read reservations or waitlist
blocked.description: Reservations, experiences, availability, waitlist, guest details, notes, preferences, allergens, special requests, visit history, messages, payments, and status remain unavailable.

blocked.label: Read table operations
blocked.description: Floor plans, tables, order progress, server rosters, rotations, covers, seating, course status, and restaurant configuration remain unavailable.

blocked.label: Change Toast Tables
blocked.description: Creating, updating, seating, messaging, charging, cancelling, deleting, publishing, or changing any reservation, waitlist, table, guest, experience, payment, or configuration remains unavailable.

blocked.label: Use raw APIs or substitute credentials
blocked.description: Arbitrary Toast APIs, raw responses, Toast Web automation, restaurant usernames or passwords, copied sessions, widget material, generic POS credentials, and standard API access as a Tables substitute are blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Provider review pending
approvalProfiles.description: No Toast Tables action is enabled until Toast approves and certifies Relay's exact Tables API, scopes, restaurant activation, guest-data, messaging, mutation, webhook, payment, and revocation contract.

providerSetup.blocker: Toast Tables stores and operates reservations, experiences, waitlists, guest profiles and notes, two-way SMS, floor plans, table and order status, server rotations, seating, prepayments, and reports. Toast's public developer guide documents general partner, custom, management-group and standard API access, but does not publish a Tables-specific API, scopes, endpoint schemas, webhook contract, sandbox workflow, or standard-access entitlement. Standard API access is read-only, has no sandbox, requires restaurant subscriptions, and exposes only its listed general APIs; it cannot be treated as implied Tables authority. Partner credentials and scopes are assigned by Toast after application review and function-specific certification, and each restaurant must activate the partner.
providerSetup.nextAction: The exclusive Toast partnership task should submit Relay's exact Tables use case and request the minimum supported reservation, waitlist and table scopes, schemas, outbound events, restaurant activation model, sandbox, and certification requirements. If Toast does not offer a supported Tables partner surface, mark this provider unsupported. If approved, store assigned client credentials only in Railway and verify token expiry, restaurant GUID binding, partner location access, per-scope denials, reservations and waitlist schemas, guest and allergen redaction, SMS consent, table state, mutation confirmations, webhook authenticity and idempotency, prepayment boundaries, rate limits, restaurant deactivation, disconnect, and post-disconnect denial before Connect is enabled.

evidence.supports: Toast documents Tables as a reservation, experience, waitlist and table-management product with guest profiles, notes, requests and visit history, two-way SMS, floor and order status, server rotations, covers, seating, prepayment and reporting.
Toast creates partner API accounts and client credentials through its integrations team; partner accounts can access only restaurants that explicitly choose the partner.
Toast uses OAuth 2 client credentials, environment-specific credentials, short-lived Bearer tokens, restaurant GUID headers, secure secret storage, and application review for partner access.

Toast assigns endpoint and operation scopes from business requirements, with some scopes available only after integration-function certification; the published scope table does not identify a Toast Tables reservation scope.
Toast's self-service Standard API access is restaurant-created, read-only, location-specific and has no sandbox, so it does not provide the required Tables mutation or certification contract.
